# Results (generated by `python -m paygap.run`)

- Employees: 588 women, 882 men
- Mean monthly income: women 6,687, men 6,381; median: women 5,082, men 4,838

| Raw (no controls) | +6.2% | -0.9% | +13.8% | 0.089 | 0.002 |
| + job level | +0.0% | -2.4% | +2.5% | 0.979 | 0.868 |
| + job role | -0.2% | -2.5% | +2.2% | 0.862 | 0.885 |
| + experience and tenure | -0.5% | -2.7% | +1.9% | 0.696 | 0.888 |
| + rating and education (full model) | -0.3% | -2.6% | +2.0% | 0.767 | 0.888 |

## Robustness

| specification | gap | ci_low | ci_high | p_value |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Full model (log pay, HC3) | -0.3% | -2.6% | +2.0% | 0.767 |
| Add age | -0.4% | -2.6% | +2.0% | 0.763 |

| Raw monthly income (not logged) | -1.0% | -2.8% | +0.7% | 0.250 |

## Oaxaca–Blinder (log points × 100)

- Raw +5.99 = explained +6.34 + unexplained -0.35
  - Job level: +4.07
  - Job role: +1.74
  - Experience: +0.58
  - Tenure: +0.04
  - Rating: -0.02
  - Education: -0.08

## Diagnostics

- Breusch–Pagan p: log pay 5.5e-19, raw pay 1.3e-17
- Correlation of job level with pay: 0.95
- VIF: TotalWorkingYears 3.11, JobLevel 2.60, YearsAtCompany 1.67, Education 1.02, PerformanceRating 1.00, female 1.00

## Promotion (ordered logit of job level)

- Odds ratio for women: 1.03 (95% CI 0.84–1.28), p = 0.754
- Women's share by level: L1 37%, L2 41%, L3 43%, L4 48%, L5 35%

## Paid ≥20% below prediction

- 200 employees flagged; rate: Female 12.1%, Male 14.6%; chi-square p = 0.187
